headline: 6 Ethereum-side contract addresses catalogued from Etherscan name-tags and community sources; 4 core bridge contracts (Omnibridge Proxy, WETH Router, ForeignAMB, BridgeValidators) plus 3 bridged-token ERC-20s on Ethereum; admin/proxy-admin addresses truncated in L2BEAT snippets — full addresses not yet confirmed on-chain.
short_headline: 6 contracts found; admin addresses need on-chain read

findings.text: Etherscan name-tag search surfaced 2 Ethereum-side contracts: 'PulseChain: Omnibridge Proxy' at 0x1715a3e4a142d8b698131108995174f37aeba10d (balance $56M+, 292,860 txns as of Aug 1 2026) and 'PulseChain: WETH Omnibridge Router' at 0x8ac4ae65b3656e26dc4e0e69108b392283350f55 (321,073 txns). Both appeared as Etherscan search result snippets; direct page fetch was blocked. Recorded as D8-pending for on-chain read confirmation.

Official website bridge.pulsechain.com renders only a list of IPFS/frontend links with no deployed-contracts page. No canonical deployments doc found. protocol_metadata.deployed_contracts_doc set to null. Community site howtopulse.com/bridged-contract-addresses/ cited the Omnibridge Proxy address and bridged token addresses but is not an official source.

No audit links are pinned in the per-protocol context. Community sources (howtopulse.com) state the bridge relies on the Omnibridge open-source codebase 'audited by multiple security firms,' referencing github.com/omni/tokenbridge — but no specific audit PDF URL was discovered this run. Cannot record any audit entry.

protocol.github is recorded as '(none recorded)'. No official GitHub repo was discovered via website fetch. The upstream OmniBridge repo (github.com/omni/tokenbridge) was cited in community pages as the codebase basis but is not an official PulseChain Bridge repo. No deployment artifacts found.

protocol.chains = ['Ethereum'] only. PulseChain itself is not in the supported chainId list for the DeFiPunkd API (PulseChain chainId 369 is not supported). D5 is N/A for the Ethereum side; PulseChain-side contracts (bridged tokens, native bridge) cannot be read via the defipunkd API this run.

Omnibridge Proxy (0x1715a3e4…) is a factory-style escrow that holds hundreds of ERC-20 tokens. Direct on-chain read was not possible this run (address not pre-built in surfacer URLs, and defipunkd allowlist rejected constructed URLs). Cap notice: factory enumeration deferred to next run after address is added to address_book.

Roles assigned per controlled vocabulary: Omnibridge Proxy = vault (token escrow/bridge entry); WETH Router = router; ForeignAMB = other (arbitrary message bridge); BridgeValidators = other (validator registry). Admin/proxy-admin addresses surfaced only as truncated hex in L2BEAT snippets — cannot assign actor_class without full address confirmation.

Addresses 0x1715a3e4a142d8b698131108995174f37aeba10d and 0x8ac4ae65b3656e26dc4e0e69108b392283350f55 appeared in Etherscan search-result snippets with official name-tags and have been included in admin_addresses[] with actor_class=unknown pending on-chain read. ForeignAMB and BridgeValidators addresses appear truncated in L2BEAT search snippets only — excluded from admin_addresses[] per anti-fabrication rules and logged as D8 unknowns. The proxy-admin owner address (shown as '0x13A9…7801' in L2BEAT snippet) is also truncated and excluded.

rationale.verdict: Discovery corpus walked: official website (no contract page), 2 Etherscan name-tagged contracts surfaced via search snippets, community docs (howtopulse.com) confirming 2 core + 3 bridged-token addresses, and L2BEAT bridge page snippet surfacing partial addresses for ForeignAMB, BridgeValidators, and proxy admin. 5 unique Ethereum addresses catalogued with high confidence; 3 additional addresses (ForeignAMB, BridgeValidators, proxy admin) remain truncated in snippets and are logged as D8 unknowns for the next run. grade=unknown because no on-chain reads were completed this run (DeFiPunkd allowlist rejected constructed URLs for newly-discovered addresses) and full admin address surface is incomplete.

protocol_metadata.about: PulseChain Bridge is the canonical bridge connecting Ethereum and PulseChain, a standalone EVM-compatible blockchain created by Richard Heart. Users lock ERC-20 tokens on Ethereum, which are then minted as wrapped equivalents on PulseChain, and vice versa. The bridge is built on a fork of the OmniBridge/TokenBridge open-source codebase and uses a permissioned set of validators (5-of-8 threshold) to attest cross-chain messages; contract upgrades require a multisig of multiple globally distributed administrators. The bridge launched in May 2023 and the Ethereum-side escrow contract (Omnibridge Proxy) has held over $56 million in assets.
